s: Network-attached disk volumes giving instances durable raw blocks - the disks behind databases.
w: Volumes attach to instances over the hypervisor fabric with provisioned IOPS/throughput. Snapshots capture point-in-time to object storage incrementally. Multi-attach enables clustered filesystems; encryption at rest is standard. Performance is guaranteed per-volume, independent of instance count.
use: Backing disks for self-managed databases (postgres/mysql data dirs)
Boot volumes for fleets with baked AMIs
High-IOPS workloads needing guaranteed throughput floors
avoid: Direct object durability/lifecycle tiers (object_storage does this better)
pits: IOPS caps surprise during peaks - alarm on burst balance
Volume detach/attach delays failover - rehearse DB failover playbooks
tips: In interviews usually implicit behind 'database'; mention explicitly when discussing disk-bound bottlenecks
